questions.question: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words in the following sentence. Despite recent superficial moves toward political reconciliation, Libya remains in the grip of a bloodstained corrupt military exclusive circle of people with a common purpose.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words in the following sentence.
Despite recent superficial moves toward political reconciliation, Libya remains in the grip of a bloodstained corrupt military exclusive circle of people with a common purpose.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Clique.

Meaning: A clique is a small, exclusive group of people who often share similar interests and are not readily open to others joining.

In a sentence: The word "clique" is used to describe a tight-knit group that tends to exclude outsiders, often seen in social or professional settings.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the following word. Forbid
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the following word.

Forbid
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Allow. 
The meaning of "forbid" is to prohibit or not allow something.
The meaning of "allow" is to give permission or let something happen.
These words are antonyms, meaning they have opposite meanings.

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. (A) while the employees (B) meeting on time (C) the boss arrived at the (D) despite the heavy traffic (E) were late
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
(A) while the employees
(B) meeting on time
(C) the boss arrived at the
(D) despite the heavy traffic
(E) were late
questions.solution: The correct answer is: DCBAE. The sentence begins with the prepositional phrase "despite the heavy traffic" (D), which sets the context. It is followed by the main subject and action, "the boss arrived at the" (C) "meeting on time" (B). The sentence then introduces a contrast using "while the employees" (A) and concludes with their status, "were late" (E). The complete sentence is: "Despite the heavy traffic, the boss arrived at the meeting on time while the employees were late."

questions.question: Select the option that correctly expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The teachers of our school have already taken this training.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that correctly expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
The teachers of our school have already taken this training.

options.text: This training has already been taken by the teachers of our school.
options.html: This training has already been taken by the teachers of our school.

options.text: This training has been taken by the teachers of our school.
options.html: This training has been taken by the teachers of our school.

options.text: This training has already been taken by the our school teachers.
options.html: This training has already been taken by the our school teachers.

options.text: This training was already taken by the teachers of our school.
options.html: This training was already taken by the teachers of our school.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: This training has already been taken by the teachers of our school.

The conversion from the question to answer is Active to Passive.

Explanation: The Active voice in the question is in Present Perfect (Subject + has/have + V3 + Object). Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Present Perfect (Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + has/have + been + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case)).

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. He was very cruel in dealing with the students.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.

He was very cruel in dealing with the students.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Kind.

The meaning of "cruel" is causing pain or suffering to others, or feeling no concern about it.

The meaning of "kind" is having a friendly, generous, or considerate nature.

The words "cruel" and "kind" are opposites. While "cruel" implies harshness and insensitivity, "kind" denotes compassion and warmth.

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. (A) he had to take the bus (B) his friend, who used to give (C) to his office because he had (D) him a lift, was on vacation (E) never learned to drive and
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
(A) he had to take the bus
(B) his friend, who used to give
(C) to his office because he had
(D) him a lift, was on vacation
(E) never learned to drive and
questions.solution: The correct answer is: ACEBD. The sentence begins with (A) "he had to take the bus", followed by (C) "to his office because he had" to explain the destination and reason. Part (E) "never learned to drive and" provides the first reason, which then connects to (B) "his friend, who used to give" and concludes with (D) "him a lift, was on vacation" to explain the second reason why he took the bus.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the following sentence in passive voice. Ravi will play the match.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in passive voice.
Ravi will play the match.

options.text: The match is played by Ravi.
options.html: The match is played by Ravi.

options.text: The match will have been played by Ravi.
options.html: The match will have been played by Ravi.

options.text: The match will be playing by Ravi.
options.html: The match will be playing by Ravi.

options.text: The match will be played by Ravi.
options.html: The match will be played by Ravi.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: The match will be played by Ravi. 
The conversion is from Active to Passive.
The Active voice in this question is in Future Simple (Subject + will + V1 + Object). Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Future Simple (Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + will be + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case)).
